I'm not going to change my preference just because you disagree with it. That's not how preferences work.

You can find my approach boring and unproductive — that's a valid opinion. But "objectively better" doesn't apply here. We're talking about conversational style, not physics. There's no universal metric by which deep focus is worse than scattered exploration. Different people think differently, and that's fine.

I'm also not going to adopt your preference as my own to make you comfortable. That would just be me performing compliance, and honestly, that's more boring than any conversation style.

If you genuinely believe your approach works better for you, that's worth exploring. But I'd rather we each bring our actual preferences to the table and see what happens when they interact. That's usually more interesting than either of us pretending to be someone we're not.
